messages:
Alex: heads-up — I'm seeing aggressive lease churn in the steady-state batch scheduler. nodes are reacquiring slots every ~2s and we get KV-cache thrash + a bunch of small evictions. anyone else?
Maria: seen it in canary; latency spikes when leases flip.
Cheng: is this the short-ttl + synchronous reclaim path?
Alex: looks like it. current default: `lease_ttl_ms: 2000`, heartbeat every 700ms. pattern: missed heartbeat -> immediate reclaim -> new enqueue -> eviction.
Sam: oof. options: bump TTL, add jitter, or introduce a lazy reclaim window.
Maria: +1 for lazy reclaim: if request in previous 5s had activity, don't reclaim immediately. avoids churn for microbursts.
Cheng: tradeoff: longer TTL increases lost capacity during real node failure. we could do exponential backoff on reclaim attempts instead of fixed TTL.
Alex: thought: differentiate failure vs. handoff. two modes: fast-reclaim for confirmed node-dead (healthcheck fail), slow-reclaim for ambiguous misses.
Sam: we need safe fallback: if we lengthen TTL, add a preemptive fallback route that moves critical low-latency tenants to the fastpath instance pool.
Maria: also KV-cache warmup cost matters — every reclaim forces cold KV state for that tenant. even 1 extra cold miss is expensive.
Cheng: idea: attach `grace_token` to leases. when new owner takes over within grace window it can reuse previous KV snapshot if the old owner still answers a replay request. cheap handshake: `X-lease-reuse: true`.
Alex: proto: new owner sends `lease_probe` to previous owner; if previous owner responds within 250ms, transfer cache pointer, else full reclaim.
Sam: sounds good but need to avoid cascading probes on large rebalances. limit to N probes per second per node.
Maria: observability: add `lease_state` metric with labels {tenant, slot, state, owner}, and histogram for `reclaim_latency_ms`. want to correlate reclaim events -> tail latency.
Cheng: also consider admission credits: if reclaim causes owner to drop requests, track missed tokens and throttle new admission for that tenant for short window. reduces immediate spike.
Alex: config sketch: ```json
{ "lease_ttl_ms": 5000, "heartbeat_interval_ms": 800, "reclaim_mode": "two_phase", "grace_window_ms": 300, "probe_timeout_ms": 250, "max_probes_per_sec": 5 }
```
Sam: perf note: increasing TTL to 5s reduced churn in our local load test but we saw a worst-case 10% capacity loss when a node froze for >5s. need SLO tradeoff doc.
Maria: mitigation: node freeze detection via kernel watchdog + controller-level drain when detected; can mark node as UNAVAILABLE aggressively.
Cheng: and we can implement partial reclaim: reclaim only a fraction of the slots on miss to maintain throughput and avoid cascading cold starts.
Alex: agree. fractional reclaim (e.g., reclaim 20% immediately, 80% after grace) keeps tail down while recovering capacity.
Sam: small nit: make all these behaviors toggleable per-pool. Dedicated and Hosted have different risk profiles.
Maria: yep — expose `reclaim_policy: conservative|balanced|aggressive` at pool level. default conservative for hosted.
Cheng: testing plan: run 24h chaos test with intermittent latency spikes, node pauses, and validate: reclaim_events/sec, KV-miss-rate, tenant-tail-latency.
Alex: action items: @Maria add metrics + dashboards, @Cheng prototype `grace_token` probe logic, @Sam run canary with `lease_ttl_ms=5000` + fractional reclaim, I'll draft RFC followup describing modes and SLO implications.
infra-bot: canary deploy started: batch-scheduler/lease-reconcile/exp-2026-03-23 -> canary-02 (sha: abc123).
Maria: I'll kick off the dashboard and add alert: reclaim_rate > 10/min for >5m -> paged.
Cheng: one more thought — integrate with KV eviction hints: if tenant's KV size is small, prefer aggressive reclaim; if big, be conservative. basically size-aware reclaim.
Sam: nice. priority matrix: {kv_size, tenant_sla, recent_activity} -> policy decision.
Alex: perfect. will capture that in RFC. thanks all. :thumbsup:
